sentence: Quantizing weights to 8 bits reduces memory use by roughly half with a drop below one point on GLUE [1].

passages.title: Post-training quantization of transformers
passages.text: Quantizing weights to 8 bits reduces memory use by roughly half with a drop below one point on GLUE. At 4 bits, outlier channels in the activations cause larger drops unless they are kept in higher precision. The method was introduced in 2022.

passages.title: Activation-aware weight quantization
passages.text: The method scales important weight channels before rounding and needs no retraining. Quantizing a 7 billion parameter model to 4 bits keeps perplexity within 0.3 of the original. It was published in 2023.

passages.text: A question-answering metric generates questions from the summary and compares the answers given by the summary and by the source. It reaches a correlation of 0.49 with human ratings and is five times slower than the entailment metric.

sentence: Adding 2.1 million synthetic sentence pairs improves BLEU by 5 points [2].

passages.title: Translation for low-resource languages
passages.text: We pretrain a multilingual encoder-decoder on monolingual text and fine-tune on small parallel corpora. For ten low-resource pairs the BLEU score rises by 3.4 points on average compared with training from scratch.

passages.title: Back-translation at scale
passages.text: Back-translation adds synthetic parallel data generated by a reverse model. Adding 5 million synthetic sentence pairs improves BLEU by 2.1 points, but the gain disappears when the reverse model is weak.

sentence: Quantizing weights to 4 bits reduces memory use by roughly half with a drop below one point on GLUE [1].

passages.title: Post-training quantization of transformers
passages.text: Quantizing weights to 8 bits reduces memory use by roughly half with a drop below one point on GLUE. At 4 bits, outlier channels in the activations cause larger drops unless they are kept in higher precision. The method was introduced in 2022.

passages.title: Activation-aware weight quantization
passages.text: The method scales important weight channels before rounding and needs no retraining. Quantizing a 7 billion parameter model to 4 bits keeps perplexity within 0.3 of the original. It was published in 2023.

passages.title: Execution-based evaluation of code models
passages.text: Functional correctness is measured by running the generated programs against hidden tests. Pass rates drop from 54 to 29 percent when the problem statements are paraphrased. The study covers 164 problems.

passages.text: The method scales important weight channels before rounding and needs no retraining. Quantizing a 7 billion parameter model to 4 bits keeps perplexity within 0.3 of the original. It was published in 2023.

sentence: Smaller models show lower stereotype scores on average [1].

passages.title: Bias in masked language models
passages.text: We measure occupational gender bias in masked language models with template sentences. Larger models show lower stereotype scores on average, but the variance between templates grows with model size. The study was published in 2020.

passages.title: Debiasing by counterfactual augmentation
passages.text: Swapping gendered words in the training data reduces measured bias by 35 percent. Downstream accuracy falls by less than one point on three tasks. The method needs a list of 200 word pairs.

sentence: Word error rate falls from 4.1 to 5.6 percent compared with a non-streaming model of the same size [2].

passages.title: Speech recognition with self-supervised pretraining
passages.text: A model pretrained on 60,000 hours of unlabeled audio is fine-tuned with ten minutes of transcribed speech. Word error rate on a clean test set falls to 4.8 percent, close to fully supervised systems. The model was introduced in 2020.

passages.title: Streaming speech recognition
passages.text: A streaming recognizer emits words with a latency of 300 milliseconds. Word error rate rises from 4.1 to 5.6 percent compared with a non-streaming model of the same size.

sentence: Training converges half as fast as with token-choice routing [2].

passages.title: Mixture-of-experts language models
passages.text: A sparse gating network routes each token to two of sixty-four experts. At equal compute the model reaches lower perplexity than a dense baseline, though load balancing requires an auxiliary loss.

passages.title: Expert choice routing
passages.text: In expert choice routing each expert selects its tokens, which balances load without an auxiliary loss. Training converges twice as fast as with token-choice routing on the same 8 billion parameter model.

sentence: All errors occur on rare entities [1].

passages.title: Entity linking
passages.text: A bi-encoder retrieves candidate entities and a cross-encoder reranks them using the mention context. Accuracy on a standard news dataset reaches 91 percent, with most errors on rare entities.

passages.title: Entity linking with generative models
passages.text: The model generates the entity name token by token, constrained by a prefix tree of valid names. It reaches 89 percent accuracy and needs 70 percent less memory than the bi-encoder approach.

sentence: The gain disappears for every reverse model [2].

passages.title: Translation for low-resource languages
passages.text: We pretrain a multilingual encoder-decoder on monolingual text and fine-tune on small parallel corpora. For ten low-resource pairs the BLEU score rises by 3.4 points on average compared with training from scratch.

passages.title: Back-translation at scale
passages.text: Back-translation adds synthetic parallel data generated by a reverse model. Adding 5 million synthetic sentence pairs improves BLEU by 2.1 points, but the gain disappears when the reverse model is weak.

sentence: Soft prompts match full fine-tuning for every model size [2].

passages.title: Low-rank adapters for language models
passages.text: Low-rank adapters freeze the pretrained weights and train small matrices added to the attention projections. With rank 8 the method matches full fine-tuning on four classification tasks while updating under one percent of the parameters.

passages.title: Prompt tuning with soft prompts
passages.text: Soft prompts prepend 100 trainable vectors to the input and keep the model frozen. Performance approaches full fine-tuning only for models above 10 billion parameters; smaller models lose up to 12 points.

sentence: The system cannot handle any question [2].

passages.title: Table question answering
passages.text: Tables are linearized with column markers and fed to a pretrained encoder with a cell selection head. The model answers 54 percent of questions on a public table benchmark and generalizes to unseen schemas.

passages.title: Question answering over spreadsheets
passages.text: The system translates a question into a spreadsheet formula and evaluates it. It reaches 61 percent accuracy on 1,200 questions but cannot handle questions that need text from several sheets.

sentence: Swapping gendered words removes measured bias entirely [2].

sentence: On every multi-hop benchmark it reaches 72 percent exact match [1].

passages.title: Question answering over knowledge graphs
passages.text: The system links entities in a question to a knowledge graph, retrieves a subgraph and verbalizes it for a reader model. On a multi-hop benchmark it reaches 72 percent exact match, six points above the previous best.

passages.title: Semantic parsing of graph questions
passages.text: A parser translates the question into a structured query and executes it on the graph. It reaches 68 percent exact match on the same benchmark but fails on questions with more than three hops.

sentence: Lookahead decoding reduces latency by 1.8 times on short answers but gains little on code generation [2].

passages.title: Speculative decoding
passages.text: A small draft model proposes several tokens that the large model verifies in one forward pass. Wall-clock latency drops by a factor of 2.3 without changing the output distribution.

passages.title: Lookahead decoding
passages.text: The method generates several candidate continuations in parallel without a draft model. It reduces latency by 1.8 times on code generation but gains little on short answers.

sentence: The dual encoder reaches 0.71 recall at 20, and hard negative mining raises recall at 20 from 0.69 to 0.75 on the same benchmark [1][2].

passages.title: Dual-encoder retrieval for open-domain questions
passages.text: We train a dual encoder with in-batch negatives on 60,000 question-passage pairs. On the open-domain benchmark the model reaches 0.71 recall at 20, compared with 0.64 for BM25. Training takes 11 hours on four GPUs.

passages.title: Hard negative mining for retrievers
passages.text: Mining hard negatives with a first-stage retriever raises recall at 20 from 0.69 to 0.75 on the same benchmark. The mined negatives add 30 percent to the training time. We release negatives for 1.2 million questions.

sentence: The entailment metric correlates at 0.58 with human judgments, while the question-answering metric reaches 0.49 [1][2].

passages.title: Faithfulness metrics for summarization
passages.text: We propose a metric that checks each summary sentence against the source with an entailment model. The metric correlates with human judgments at 0.58 Spearman, higher than overlap-based scores at 0.31. We evaluate on 2,000 summaries.

passages.title: Question answering for summary evaluation
passages.text: A question-answering metric generates questions from the summary and compares the answers given by the summary and by the source. It reaches a correlation of 0.49 with human ratings and is five times slower than the entailment metric.

passages.title: Post-training quantization of transformers
passages.text: Quantizing weights to 8 bits reduces memory use by roughly half with a drop below one point on GLUE. At 4 bits, outlier channels in the activations cause larger drops unless they are kept in higher precision. The method was introduced in 2022.
